Web design in El Paso starts with knowing it is not like the rest of Texas

El Paso is far enough west that it keeps a different clock from Dallas and Houston, and different enough in every other way that a website written for "Texas" usually misses it. Good web design in El Paso has to fit a city of nearly 680,000 people, by the Census Bureau's 2023 estimate, where about 81 percent of residents are Hispanic or Latino, per the same Census estimates, and about two in three speak a language other than English at home.

Dominion Web Design Pro builds sites for El Paso businesses with that in mind. Maurice Johnson researches your part of the city, writes every page by hand for your business, and builds a demo you can look at before paying a cent.

The work is remote, from Big Sandy in East Texas. What matters on the page is not where it was typed but whether it speaks to the person in Northeast El Paso or the Lower Valley who is about to pick up the phone.

What drives business in El Paso

The Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas names Fort Bliss as El Paso's largest employer and an important generator of local economic activity. Transportation and logistics matter too, because of the border and the city's trading relationship with Ciudad Juárez, which makes El Paso one of the major crossing points on the U.S.-Mexico border. Manufacturing across the river feeds El Paso's service businesses as well.

That mix produces a particular set of small businesses. Military families moving in and out need movers, mechanics, home services, child care and dentists, and they search for them fast because they are new in town. Logistics and trade create work for trucking companies, repair shops, and the restaurants and offices around them. And a large, settled bilingual population supports the salons, clinics, contractors and family restaurants that every neighborhood has.

The geography adds its own pattern. Kern Place, just east of the University of Texas at El Paso and west of downtown, mixes older homes with a small entertainment district at its edges, and North Mesa Street carries offices and retail through that side of town. Montana Avenue's central stretch, once a row of grand homes, has been turning into a commercial corridor, and farther east the road runs out through fast-growing Far East El Paso. A business on the Westside and one on the Eastside can share a city and still serve almost entirely different customers.

Writing an El Paso website for a bilingual city

According to Census estimates for 2019 to 2023, 66.4 percent of El Paso residents five or older use a language besides English in their homes. That does not mean every page has to be translated, and it does not mean English is a barrier for most customers. It means the people reading your site move between two languages all day, and they notice whether a business seems to welcome both.

  • Say it on the page. If your staff speaks Spanish, say so near the top. "Se habla español" on a contractor's home page answers a question before it is asked.
  • Use the words people search. Some customers search in English, some in Spanish, many in a mix. Your service names should match how your customers actually talk.
  • Keep it simple on a phone. Short sentences, clear buttons and a visible phone number help every reader.
  • Mind the clock. Hours listed on your site should be El Paso time. Out-of-town customers calling from Central Time will appreciate the clarity.

On demand: the Ubersuggest data behind this site counts about 880 monthly searches for "web design El Paso" at an SEO difficulty of 14, the strongest Texas city search in that data outside Houston, Dallas and Austin. Plenty of El Paso owners are looking. The same is true of their customers.

Fort Bliss families add one more wrinkle: many of them are searching for a business before they even arrive, from another state, trying to line up movers, child care or a mechanic ahead of time. Pages that explain what you do and where you work, without assuming the reader knows the city, serve those customers well.

A note on working together across the state. Big Sandy runs on Central Time, El Paso on Mountain, so a 9 a.m. call in El Paso is 10 a.m. in East Texas. In practice that rarely matters: the demo arrives as a link you open whenever you like, photos and details go by text or email, and page approvals happen on your schedule.

Straight answer on location: Dominion Web Design Pro has no office in El Paso. Maurice Johnson builds every site from Big Sandy in East Texas and delivers it remotely, by link, phone and email.

Free business help in El Paso

None of these is connected to Dominion Web Design Pro. They are listed because they help.

SCORE El Paso

Free, confidential mentoring from volunteer business professionals, in person, by email or by video, plus low-cost workshops and webinars. El Paso is now served through SCORE's Central Texas chapter, so check the site for current meeting places.

El Paso Hispanic Chamber of Commerce

Focused on small, minority, veteran and women-owned businesses. It has operated El Paso's federally funded MBDA Business Center, and it helps owners with business plans, marketing plans and access to capital. Federal funding for these centers changed in 2025, so call ahead about current services.

City of El Paso Economic Development

The city's business services team publishes small business resources in English and Spanish for owners starting and growing in El Paso.

The package that fits your El Paso business

A neighborhood salon, taqueria or shop that needs to be found, called and visited fits Starter, a five-page site with a page about your service area, typically finished in seven to fourteen days. A contractor, cleaner or mobile service covering several parts of the city fits Pro, where the 10 city pages carry the neighborhood and suburb searches. A company with several services across the region, from Las Cruces to the Lower Valley, fits Agency, where the research comes first and decides which place-and-service pages are worth writing.

Common questions

What should an El Paso small business budget for a website?

Plan on a one-time build price plus a small monthly cost for hosting. Here the build is $497 (Starter, five pages), $997 (Pro, ten pages and ten city pages) or $1,997 (Agency, keyword research first and then a page for every place and service the research supports). Hosting, maintenance and updates run $49 a month, and they come bundled if you keep the AI agent instead.

Should my El Paso business website be in Spanish too?

Roughly two in three El Paso residents over age five use a language besides English at home, by Census count, so it is worth deciding early. Many El Paso customers read English comfortably but trust a business more when it plainly welcomes Spanish speakers. Mention how your customers talk in your demo request, and Maurice will explain honestly what your package can cover.

Do you work with El Paso businesses even though you are in East Texas?

Yes. Maurice works from Big Sandy and hands the site over by link, phone and email. One practical note: El Paso is on Mountain Time, an hour behind East Texas, so calls get scheduled with that in mind. The free demo works the same from anywhere.

Can my website cover Horizon City, Socorro or Las Cruces too?

If you serve them, yes. The Pro package includes 10 city pages, each researched and written for that place, so a contractor working the Eastside, Horizon City, Socorro and across the state line in Las Cruces can have a real page for each.

Who answers the phone when I call about an El Paso website?

An AI receptionist answers (903) 636-7511 any hour. Mention a website preview, or say you want Maurice or a real person, and the call goes through to him.
